name: Measles & vaccine-preventable
value: US, Mexico, Bolivia lose elimination (17 Nov)
summary: PAHO confirmed on 17 Nov that the US, Mexico and Bolivia lost measles elimination; 58,213 cases in Americas in 2026
state: PAHO announced on 17 Nov that its re-verification commission, meeting 10–13 Nov, concluded that the United States, Mexico and Bolivia have lost measles elimination status after a year or more of continuous transmission; the three must submit corrective plans (PAHO; Health Policy Watch). The Americas recorded 58,213 cases and 114 deaths in 2026 to 6 Nov (PAHO). The CDC counted 5,412 US cases to 12 Nov, the most since 1991 (Latin Times, citing CDC). Loss of elimination status meets Watch; the Alert line on rising deaths is not clearly crossed.
for_you: Measles spreads easily and can be serious. The NHS advises checking that you and your children have had two doses of the MMR vaccine; FCDO travel advice and NHS fit for travel list outbreak destinations.
rubric_hit: Watch: loss of elimination status (PAHO, 17 Nov: US, Mexico, Bolivia); Americas 58,213 cases, 114 deaths in 2026

why: Falling vaccination rates are bringing back diseases once eliminated; measles is the canary for the rest.

rubric.alert: Multi-country surge with rising deaths, or polio/diphtheria resurgence in high-income countries.
rubric.watch: Large outbreaks in high-income countries, or loss of elimination status.
rubric.normal: No large outbreaks in high-income countries.
